rules.text: The `rules` block has two halves: these shipped rows, and a user's own rows in `.claude/routing.local.json`, which follow them, and a user's row wins where the two disagree on the same point, so read both files before a seat pick. That file's `classes` entries merge over this table's rows through `routing_layers.py`, so read a class through `throttle.py resolve`, not from this file alone.
Every routing-table update keeps the current model round's experience reusable for the next (stable task kinds and seat tests apart from the dated model mapping, with a per-generation changelog).
xhigh is the default for most work, and important, long-chain, essential or hard work takes max, with its reason given; the rule is not rigid (owner, 2 and 3 October 2026).

A reviewing seat takes the other model family from the author by default, a soft rule that never outranks performance, efficiency, effectiveness, limits (a family at its limit now, never one expected to reach it) or the owner's explicit word.

The test, applied to the task in hand: a closed and precise brief → the anchor (`xhigh` for the closed-task classes builder, verifier, wiki-compile, memory-hunter and planner), or `high` for a closed one-leg task; on opus `max` only after an `xhigh` attempt failed, or for a genuinely hard or very extensive task, because max is slow and costly (owner ruling 2026-09-22 19:0x BST, which moved the `critic` and `reflector` Claude-half anchors from `max` to `xhigh`: `max` for a framework-changing or extensive review, `xhigh` for a narrow second pass); `gate-judge` is fixed at the executor's default tier.

A model below the anchor only where the instructions are clear and a mistake is unlikely; `gate-judge` none, since a gate measures the routed step at its default tier and a second gate lane is a fresh spawn, never a resume.

opus (Opus 5.5) by default for every build, the closed-work model; xhigh the anchor, max only after a failed xhigh attempt or for a genuinely hard or very extensive build; sonnet per call under the delegate skill §2 test, the reason recorded (owner ruling 2026-11-01).
per call: opus whenever relevance needs judgement, sonnet only for a closed one-leg lookup with the reason recorded (delegate skill §2 rule of 2026-09-06); the default is opus (Opus 5.5) at xhigh.

per call: opus whenever the claims may need reasoning rather than lookup, a lower model only for a closed mechanical list with the reason recorded; verification is closed work, so opus (Opus 5.5) at xhigh, max only after a failed xhigh or for a genuinely hard or very extensive claim list (delegate skill §2 rules of 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-22).

opus (Opus 5.5) by default for every compile, the closed-work model (sonnet per call under the delegate skill §2 test, the reason recorded; owner ruling 2026-11-01), at xhigh, max only after a failed xhigh or for a genuinely hard or very extensive paper.

preset_model._: Presets select the configured model; the effort axis follows each preset rule.

codex.note: the Codex half of the critic, admitted by the owner ruling of 2026-09-22 19:0x; since the owner ruling of 2026-10-23 a review of open work (a framework change, a design or a plan) sits on the Claude half, opus 5.5, and this half serves a closed review of opus-built work by the family rule, and ultra is retired, opus at max being the top step for every seat, on the owner's answer of 2 November 2026; spawned through codex-lane.py with --class critic and --stage-from the artefact copy (the throttle does not resolve it; every pick carries --choice-reason); read-only; the Claude half serves closed reviews, a build against a written spec or a claim list

_: Model and effort defaults are anchors for per-call selection; record a reason for each override.
